thread:
Maya (PM): proposing a phased rollout plan for tenant-priority feature. goal: safe ramp for top 50 paying tenants, minimal perf regression, clear SLA carveouts. thoughts? :thinking_face:
Ryan (SRE): +1 on carveouts. need explicit latency & error SLOs per-slice. suggest start with 0.5% global traffic + 10% of top-tenants (by qps) as canary.
Sofia (Backend): agree. recommend hybrid canary: region-based warmup + tenant holdback bucket. this avoids noisy neighbors.
Maya (PM): sketching the phases: 1) internal alpha (internal apps) 2) hybrid canary (region warm + 10 tenants) 3) customer A/B (50 tenant cohort vs control) 4) staged regional rollout. rollback criteria at each phase.
Leo (AE): need a customer-facing SLA note. sales will ask: what happens to committed SLAs during canary? can we opt specific customers out?
Maya (PM): yes — opt-out path for enterprise customers. propose add flag: "priority_opt_out" per-tenant. sample flag config below:
```
feature_flags:
  tenant_priority:
    enabled: true
    rollout:
      phase1: { type: "internal" }
      phase2: { type: "hybrid-canary", tenants: ["t-123","t-456"], regions: ["us-east-1"] }
      phase3: { type: "ab", split: 0.5 }
    fallback: "downgrade-to-lite-model"
```
Sofia (Backend): +1. Also add automatic fallback policy: if p95 latency > 350ms for 3m or error rate > 0.8% for 5m, route affected traffic to baseline model variant and alert SRE. ops-bot can wire that.
ops-bot: create incident if threshold breached, runpoint: @Ryan (SRE), fallback action: set flag tenant_priority=false for affected tenant(s).
Ryan (SRE): technical note — need token-budget guard for high-throughput tenants. also rate-limit backpressure and circuit-breaker per-tenant to prevent cascade.
Maya (PM): good catch. add per-tenant concurrency cap and token budget. also include a telemetry panel: per-tenant latency, token-usage, model-variant, errors, and choice of fallback reason.
Leo (AE): quick ask from sales: can we promise a hotfix window if a large customer opts out then requests re-enable during a surge? they expect 2-4 hour turnaround.
Sofia (Backend): operationally possible but needs runbook & on-call commitment. we should mark as "surgical re-enable" requiring on-call approval.
Maya (PM): acceptance criteria for GA: - autopilot fallback in place - telemetry dashboards live - opt-out path documented + SLA clause - successful AB with <0.5% customer-impact regressions - runbook & rollback script tested in staging.
Sofia (Backend): testing checklist: shadow traffic run for 24h (no activation), synthetic QPS spike test, failure-injection (model oom) validating fallback, and A/B metric collection.
Ryan (SRE): schedule a staged warmup window: 00:00-04:00 UTC for region priming, and a kill-switch toggle. ops-bot will post deploy-heartbeat during rollout windows.
Maya (PM): action items: @Sofia create rollout flag PR + sample config, @Ryan add circuit-breaker + ops-bot rule, @Leo draft customer SLA addendum, I'll own prod runbook and GA criteria doc. target: start hybrid canary next Tues.
Leo (AE): I'll queue customers for opt-in and notify CS.
Sofia (Backend): PR incoming today, will include `curl` snippet for quick rollback:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/flags \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"tenant":"t-123","flag":"tenant_priority","value":false}'
```
Maya (PM): perfect. if no blockers I'll schedule the shiproom review. thanks all :rocket:
Ryan (SRE): thumbs up. one more: add a canary kill-switch metric to surface in console (big red). saved our bacon before. :+1:
